- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after a spike), so reduce forecast by 5–15% for the next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >15% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 10–20% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to hold or over-forecast — adjust downward by 5–10% for 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — cap forecast at 1.2x recent 14-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model fails to recognize it — reduce forecast by 10–20% for 3–5 days following such drop.
